# Onboarding, the reading path

This repo holds five months of Scribl material and no map. This page is the map.
It is ordered by the question you are trying to answer, not by folder. Each stop
names a file, says why it is worth your time, and gives a rough read time. Stops
marked SKIP FIRST PASS are worth knowing about and not worth reading today.

Two warnings before you start.

Documents here span 2026-07-14 to the present and several are superseded without
saying so on the page. Where two documents disagree, this page says which one is
current. Read the section "What contradicts what" before you trust anything you
find by searching.

Source files live in `product/`, `tracking/`, `handbook/` and `knowledge/`. The
pages under `docs/` are rendered copies produced by `npm run docs:sync` from
`scripts/docs-sync.mjs`. Read the source, edit the source. The old `s2d` tree
some earlier documents still name was rehomed into those four; a path starting
with it is stale.

Full path, about 3 hours. Fifteen-minute path, see the last section.

## What is this product and who is it for

1. `product/context/documents/scribl-d2c-mlp-prfaq.md`, 15 min. The product thesis in
   the client's own framing, written as a press release and FAQ. One AI-generated
   prompt a day, answered with a drawing, text or voice, shared to private
   channels. Q4 in that file, "Do I need to be a good artist? Absolutely not",
   is the whole positioning in one line. The file is marked "Confidential,
   Internal Working Document" at the top, so treat its dates and pricing lines as
   draft, not as commitments.
2. `product/design/poc-realignment-plan.md`, 25 min, the single highest-value read on
   this list. Written 2026-08-20 against the client's own Figma frames and sales
   deck. It carries the current screen order, the reduced canvas, the design
   decisions we are waiting on, and in section 7 a paste-ready client summary.
3. `product/context/documents/scribl-d2c-mvp-scope.md`, 10 min. SKIP FIRST PASS
   unless you are shaping scope. Overlaps the PRFAQ and predates the kickoff.

## What exists today, POC and infrastructure

4. `product/inputs/scribl-live-screens-2026-07-20/`, 5 min. Seven screenshots of the
   running POC signed in as a real account. This is what the app actually looks
   like today. Everything else labelled "design" is intent.
5. `product/design/figma-exports/`, 10 min. The 23 frames the client sent. These are
   flow truth and not visual truth. They are wireframes on a `#1E1E1E` ground and
   copying that dark chrome as the app theme would be wrong, per
   `product/design/poc-realignment-plan.md` section 6.
6. `tracking/production-backend-plan.md`, 20 min. What the backend actually is for
   this build. API Gateway plus Lambda, Aurora Serverless v2, one region, no AI
   lanes in the MVP. It is also the only file that names the open architecture
   divergences honestly, so read it before the ADRs.
7. `product/context/pages/reference/poc/architecture/README.md`, 15 min. The target
   AWS architecture with the canonical diagram, EKS and Bedrock and multi-region.
   This is the 30-month destination, not what is being built in the next eight
   weeks. Read it to understand what the MVP is a cut of. Skip the cost tables,
   see the exclusions note below.
8. The code, which is not in this repository and is not a submodule. Clone the
   repositories as siblings of this one: the production build in Scribl's own
   GitHub organisation (confirm the org and repository name on the team channel,
   it is not recorded here yet), and `scribl-app`, the POC, which is reference
   only and must not be ported from. `scribl-b2b`, the client's existing B2B
   product, is a useful third read for how their stack actually works.

## What we are building in the next eight weeks, and what we are not

9. `tracking/backlog-epics.md`, 30 min, the plan of record. Fifteen epics, the
   band mapping against the 2026-08-19 kickoff board, and the capacity
   arithmetic. Eight weeks from 2026-08-24, two discovery weeks then three
   two-week sprints. Green band is E01 to E07, the daily loop plus QA foundation
   plus build and signing. Orange is E08 to E11. Gray is E12 to E14, each with a
   named later home. E15 is parked capability, meaning already built and switched
   off.
10. `tracking/open-questions.md`, 20 min. Sixty-two numbered questions, of which
    forty-five are open and seventeen are answered and kept on the page so the
    record shows the list being worked down. Every one has a named owner and sits
    in the group matching what it blocks. Group A is blocking work running right
    now. The client-facing extract at the end of the file is the subset already
    vetted to send to Scribl. Its code-blocking subset, with the architect's
    working positions attached, is `handbook/engineering/code-questions.md`.
11. `tracking/production-sprint-backlog.md`, SKIP FIRST PASS. Superseded
    2026-08-20 and banner-marked as such. Useful only as the story-level
    Fibonacci sizing history.
12. `tracking/production-backlog.md` and `tracking/expo-rebuild-epics.md`, SKIP
    FIRST PASS. Long-horizon inventory from 2026-07-10 and 2026-07-27. Feature
    rows in `tracking/backlog-epics.md` cite the RE epics they carry forward, so
    you get what you need from there.
13. `handbook/backlog-and-workflow.md`, 10 min. How work flows here, and the
    mandatory rule that a change in a code repository updates its story in
    `tracking/stories/` in the same unit of work. Then
    `handbook/engineering/index.md`, 5 min, which is the reading order for the
    production build's engineering documentation: the decision register, the
    architecture and its enforced boundaries, the toolchain, CI/CD, release
    readiness, developer setup, feature flags, and the blocking questions. That
    section is the single copy of those documents; nothing in the build
    repository duplicates them. The rest of `handbook/` is generic agile
    process, SKIP FIRST PASS.

## Why the architecture is what it is

The eleven ADRs live in `product/inputs/reference/decisions/`. Read the README index
first, 5 min, then these four, 15 min total. All eleven are still formally
"Proposed" and none was promoted to "Accepted".

Still binding.

- `0001-react-native-primary.md`. One React Native and TypeScript codebase.
  Confirmed by the shipped app.
- `0004-dynamodb-single-table.md`. Despite the filename, the decision was revised
  to Aurora Serverless v2 Postgres as the system of record, with DynamoDB kept as
  a forward-scale option. Confirmed current by `tracking/production-backend-plan.md`.
- `0005-aws-cdk-iac.md`. All infrastructure as CDK TypeScript.
- `0006-drawing-canvas-skia.md`. React Native Skia for the canvas. The voice half
  of this ADR is unresolved, see Q18.
- `0007-submit-to-unlock-data-layer.md`. Submit-to-unlock is enforced server side
  as a transactional check, restated as a load-bearing invariant in the backend
  plan. This is the product's core rule, read this one.

Superseded or contradicted, read them knowing that.

- `0002-serverless-first-backend.md` and `0003-ai-pipeline-separate-service.md`
  put the AI pipeline on ECS Fargate as a separate service.
  `product/context/pages/reference/poc/architecture/our-enhancement-pipeline.md`
  shows the shipped path is a Lambda in the same deploy, and
  `tracking/production-backend-plan.md` says no AI lanes run in the MVP at all.
- `0008-analytics-separate-pipeline.md` chose Kinesis, S3 and Athena. PostHog is
  the MLP analytics system of record per
  `product/inputs/reference/technical-implementation-plan.md` section 6 and the
  backend plan. The ADR flags itself as under review.
- `0010-async-ai-pipeline.md` holds in principle, submit never blocks on AI, but
  the mechanism described in
  `product/context/pages/reference/poc/architecture/our-enhancement-pipeline.md` is
  an un-awaited call from the submit handler and not the SQS queue the ADR
  describes.
- `0009-claude-provider-abstraction.md` and `0011-model-tiering.md` describe the
  Claude seam and the Opus, Sonnet, Haiku split. Both are sound and neither is
  exercised yet, because no AI lane ships in the MVP.

14. `tracking/future-scale-track.md`, 10 min. SKIP FIRST PASS unless you are on
    architecture. It is the bridge between the MVP and the target, and it names
    the largest open gap in the corpus, the 100k-concurrent demo wall.

## Who is on the team, and who decides what

15. `knowledge/team/roster.md`, 10 min. Both sides, with roles and the gaps stated.
    Read the version on branch `scribl-roster-refresh` if it has not merged yet,
    see the contradictions section.
16. `knowledge/meetings/2026-08-19-kickoff.md`, 15 min. The client kickoff. Scope
    at roughly one third of the SOW, eight weeks, iOS only, Wednesday demo
    cadence, Jira, client-curated prompts stay client-curated.
17. `knowledge/meetings/2026-07-14-workshop.md`, 15 min. Where the eight key
    product decisions were made and the timeline was reset onto re:Invent in
    December 2026. Comments were removed from the product in this room.
18. `knowledge/meetings/2026-08-20-kickoff-walkthrough.md`, 15 min. Internal only.
    The delivery team's first look, and the source of every iOS shipping question
    in group A of the open questions page.
19. `knowledge/meetings/2026-08-18-alignment.md`, SKIP FIRST PASS. Internal, and
    its team table is stale, see below.

Who decides what, as it actually works today. Eric Rice owns backlog and scope
decisions with a roughly two business day turnaround, and no product owner is
named on paper, which is Q22. Christina owns design answers. Matthew Kaplan is
the CEO and signs. On our side Rob Forshier is the engagement lead, Pankaj
Aggarwal is engineering lead and architect and is not full time, Pramod Kumar
runs delivery, and there is no PM, which is Q25.

## What is still open

20. `tracking/open-questions.md`, group A first, 10 min, then
    `handbook/engineering/code-questions.md`, 10 min, which is the subset that
    blocks somebody writing code this week and carries the architect's position
    on each. If you read one thing before a client call, read group A and the
    client-facing extract.

The shape of it. The iOS shipping track is the hottest, Q44 to Q48 and Q5, and
none of it can move until Scribl provisions an Apple Developer account. The
design track, Q1 to Q4, is blocking theme work in flight. AWS account ownership
and who pays for hosting, Q17 and Q49, are not blocking today and become urgent
the moment backend work is funded. Q48, the testing bar, is called the largest
uncosted item on the page and it is ours to settle, not the client's.

## What to ignore

Ranked by how much time it saves you.

- `product/context/future-architecture-aws.md` and
  `knowledge/research/scribl-poc-aws-architecture.md` are near-verbatim
  generated mirrors of
  `product/context/pages/reference/poc/architecture/README.md` and its cost model.
  Read the README, ignore the mirrors.
- `product/context/pages/reference/*` are generated copies of
  `product/inputs/reference/*`. The inputs are the source.
- `docs/*` are generated copies of `product/*`, `tracking/*`, `handbook/*` and
  `knowledge/*`. There are no exceptions any more: the open-questions register
  and this page were hand-authored under `docs/` until 2026-08-31 and are now
  ordinary sources like everything else. `reviews/` is repo-only and is not
  rendered at all.
- `handbook/definition-of-done.md`, `estimation.md` and `ceremonies.md` are
  Confluence boilerplate with no Scribl content in them yet.

Three things this repo should fix, which are findings and not edits made here.
`tracking/stories/S-020-family-challenges.md` needs a pointer to the E15 parking
decision. ADR 0003 still reads as a live decision while the backend plan and the
enhancement-pipeline page disagree with it about where the AI pipeline runs; 0002
and 0008 were given superseded banners on 2026-08-31 and 0003 was not, because
nobody has actually decided it. Two AWS estimate workbooks exist with different
contents, `product/inputs/scribl-d2c-aws-estimate-v3.xlsx` and
`product/inputs/reference/poc/architecture/Scribl-D2C-AWS-Estimate-v3.xlsx`, and one
of them is stale.

## Fifteen minutes before a client call

Read section 7 of `product/design/poc-realignment-plan.md`, which is a paste-ready
summary of where the design stands and what we need from them. Then read the
client-facing extract at the end of `tracking/open-questions.md`, which is the
twenty-four questions already vetted to ask Scribl, ordered by urgency. Then skim
the board mapping table in `tracking/backlog-epics.md`, which tells you what is
in the eight weeks and what has a later home. That is enough to answer what we
are building, what we are waiting on, and who owes us an answer. Do not quote
cost figures, the SOW fee, or anything from `reviews/`, none of it is
client-facing.
